Name: Breadth is not cost
Description: Touching many layers, files, or services is nearly free — a capable model traverses a system quickly. Never point a story up because it spans the stack.

Name: Novelty is cost
Description: Work with no precedent to copy requires decisions, and decisions require a human.

Name: Verification is cost
Description: Work you cannot prove correct with a test costs real time no matter how fast it was written.

Name: Feature story
Description: The default for all feature work. A story with no flags changes existing machinery by following a pattern already in the codebase. That is most stories. There is no separate trivial tier.

Name: Recent bug fix (within last few weeks)
Description: Bugs discovered shortly after the feature was shipped. Older bugs beyond that window receive standard feature story points.

Name: Precedent test
Condition: Name the file (or screen) in this codebase that already does this
Description: Used by the decision-density and design flags. Can name it → derivable, flag does not apply. Cannot name it → someone has to decide, flag applies. Cite the precedent in the story's Architecture Notes.

Name: Decision density
Condition: No precedent, but the shape is bounded
Description: A new table, a documented read-only third-party endpoint, a job modelled on an existing job. Never fires on breadth alone: a story crossing schema, service, controller and view scores nothing here if each layer has a precedent.

Name: Decision density
Condition: No precedent AND orchestrating an outcome in a system you do not control
Description: An external write with partial-failure semantics, or anything needing compensation, idempotency, or unwinding. Third-party work has no flag of its own — orchestrating a new dependency scores here; reading and rendering a documented endpoint usually scores nothing.

Name: Design
Condition: Creates a primary view AND you can name an existing screen whose layout it copies
Description: Work is real (what fields, what copy, what each row shows) but bounded. A new section, page, modal, or list-plus-form in an established design system. A whole new screen always scores at least 2x.

Name: Design
Condition: Creates a primary view AND you cannot name a precedent, OR the interaction is novel
Description: Multi-step wizard, drag-and-drop, live-updating surface, animation-led UI, an entirely new user journey. Also when the spec asks for design exploration or multiple layout options. Recommend splitting into a design story plus an implementation story at this tier only.

Name: Design
Description: Edge states only, wiring already-designed components to data, copy or toggle changes, adding a field or column, a read-only addition following the pattern beside it.

Name: Primary vs edge states
Description: Count only primary states — what the feature exists to show and do. Never count edge states: empty, loading, submitting, validation errors, API errors, confirm dialogs, disabled states. An eight-state form is not four times a two-state one because six of those are edge.

Name: Verification
Condition: A passing test cannot prove this story works
Description: Correctness depending on production-shaped data, background jobs on a cron cadence, eventual consistency, migrations and backfills, and anywhere the test suite mocks the very thing under test.

Name: Communication
Condition: Requires domain experts, client coordination, real-time alignment, or third-party provider coordination (Coinbase, Alchemy, etc.)
Description: Ambiguous domain rules, stakeholder sign-off, cross-team handoffs, third-party support or approval. Waiting on a human is still waiting on a human.

Name: Formula
Description: points = base × decisionDensity(1|2|4) × design(1|2|4) × verification(1|2) × communication(1|2)

Name: Typical values
Description: Anything reaching 16 should almost certainly be split. Bug fixes stay at 0.

Name: Default to 1
Description: A story earns its way up by tripping a flag. If you cannot name which flag applies and why, it is a 1.

Name: Never charge the same difficulty twice
Description: If story A builds a mechanism and story B consumes it, only A carries the flag. Name the owning story in B's notes.

Name: Kind not amount
Description: A score prices the kind of hard, not the amount of surface. A 2-pt story can still be the riskiest thing in the build — add a Risk note rather than inflating the number.

Name: Split on kinds of hard
Description: Split when a story carries two different flags, or when the score reaches 8 unless the flags are inseparable. Never split by file count.

Name: Never split a layer from its only consumer
Description: A schema whose only reader is one API, and an API whose only consumer is one screen, are one story. Exceptions: a destructive migration you want verified first, a schema with multiple consumers landing at different times, or a backfill that must run before its reader exists.
